title: Claude same-scope tie is decided by list order: an enabled ancestor local row masks a disabled deeper one
description: From lore-cli via opum-agent OPAG-448 AC3 (2)(b); opum-agent reports ruling 29 makes the deepest-projectPath rule binding (not yet read on opum-doc by this session). lore-cli fix: opum-ai/lore-cli#291, dev dc09ca98, src/adapters/agent-plugins.ts decodeClaudePluginList: between two applicable rows of the SAME scope, the deeper projectPath wins; a row with no projectPath is least specific. MEASURED HERE 2026-09-26 at origin/dev f21783a, quest agents --check --target claude run in <outer>/inner with a fake claude listing two local rows, <outer> enabled:true and <outer>/inner enabled:false. Outer row listed first: state installed, remedy claude plugin update. Inner row listed first: state disabled. decodeClaude in src/adapters/agents/cli-agent-plugins.ts replaces only on a strictly lower rank, so the first row listed wins a tie.

acceptanceCriteria.text: Between applicable Claude rows of the same scope, the one with the deeper projectPath decides, independent of list order; a row without projectPath is least specific
A test covers both row orders and asserts the same state (disabled) for each
The fix is cited against lore-cli dc09ca98 and the opum-doc record of ruling 29, and bun run check exits 0

plan: 1. decodeClaude tracks the canonical projectPath length as depth; a row replaces the current one on a lower scope rank, or on the same rank with greater depth; no projectPath is depth 0
2. Test via the real CLI with a fake claude, both list orders, the mirror case, the no-projectPath case, and rank-before-depth; mutation controls
implementationNotes: IMPLEMENTED on fix/qcli-379-claude-scope-depth-tiebreak off origin/dev e3efadb. Ruling 29 is recorded as opum-doc ADR Amendment 6 (ODOC-286, commit 44326c5, opum-ai/opum-doc#458, an ancestor of opum-doc main 7818aca, read directly there): within one scope the deepest applicable projectPath decides, never row order. CHANGE src/adapters/agents/cli-agent-plugins.ts decodeClaude: depth is the canonical projectPath length (both paths are ancestors of, or equal to, the project, so longer means deeper); a row with no projectPath is depth 0, the least specific; rank still decides first. This is the same rule as lore-cli dc09ca98 decodeClaudePluginList. TESTS test/qcli379-claude-scope-depth-tiebreak.test.ts, 4 cases through the real CLI, each asserting both list orders: an enabled ancestor over a disabled deeper row reads disabled; the mirror reads installed (so the rule is depth, not disabled-wins); a same-scope row with no projectPath loses; a local ancestor still beats a deeper project row. CONTROLS, predicted, both exact: M1 no tie-break, 3/4 red (cases 1-3); M2 depth ranked before scope, 1/4 red (case 4). The filing measurement (outer-first read installed) is case 1 order ab. bun run check exit 0, 671 pass. Ruling 28 (managed first) is NOT in this change: it is QCLI-381.
